Order 
The present application under Section 483(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 has been filed by the applicant seeking cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to respondent No.2 by order dated 20.06.2025 passed in Bail Application No. 1580 of 2025 by the Court of 12th Additional Sessions Judge, Gwalior, in connection with Crime No. 74 of 2024 registered at Police Station Crime Branch, District Gwalior, for offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the IPC.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that serious allegations of criminal conspiracy, forgery,
impersonation, and fraudulent withdrawal of funds through fabricated documents have been levelled against respondent No.2.

The complainant, who operates a DTDC courier business,
discovered on 01.08.2024, while checking his credit score online, that a housing loan of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31636 2 MCRC-28139-2025 Rs.30,00,000/- had been disbursed in his name by LIC Housing Finance Limited without his knowledge, authority, or consent.
During the course of investigation, the role of accused Hitendra Soni, serving as Area Manager at the Gwalior branch of LIC Housing Finance, came under serious scrutiny.

Under the internal structure and Standard Operating Procedures of the institution, the Area Manager is the primary authority entrusted with initial verification of documents, physical inspection of the property, and Sanjeev Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173547888/

sentences.text: recommending loan proposals to the head office.
It is his statutory and procedural duty to ensure due verification of borrower credentials and physical verification of mortgaged property prior to processing high-value loan proposals.
In the present case, forged documents were never verified as per protocol, and the accused forwarded incomplete and defective files, thereby facilitating the fraudulent disbursal of the loan.
His conduct caused wrongful loss to the financial institution and wrongful gain to the beneficiaries of the fabricated loan transactions.

It is further submitted that the investigation revealed deliberate withholding of crucial information by the accused, non-production of essential files despite repeated summons, and evasive conduct during the inquiry.
Even when he eventually appeared for interrogation, his responses regarding missing documents and procedural lapses were unsatisfactory.
The case diary indicates that documents pertaining to the fraudulent loan accounts were destroyed or concealed.

Despite the seriousness of the charges and the accused's suspected active involvement, respondent No.2 filed an anticipatory bail application before the learned Sessions Court, asserting NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:31636 3 MCRC-28139-2025 false implication and concocted allegations.

The Sessions Court, by order dated 20.06.2025, granted anticipatory bail to the accused without appreciating the gravity of the economic offence, the nature of the financial fraud involved, and the far-reaching consequences of allowing a key conspirator to remain at large.

The Court placed undue reliance on the self- serving statements of the accused while disregarding the documentary evidence collected during investigation and the statements of senior LIC officers assigning responsibility to him.
Granting him liberty at such a crucial stage undermines the ongoing investigation and sends an inappropriate message in matters involving white-collar crimes and financial misconduct.
On these grounds, it is prayed that the present application be allowed and that the anticipatory bail granted to respondent No.2 be cancelled.

On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that after grant of anticipatory bail by the learned trial Court, the respondent cooperated fully with the investigation and never violated any condition of the order.
No complaint has been made by the police authorities alleging non-cooperation or breach of bail conditions after 20.06.2025.
Hence, the present application is devoid of merit and deserves dismissal.
It is further submitted that the learned trial Court granted anticipatory bail after considering the submissions of the parties and perusing the case diary in detail.
Thereafter, the respondent continued to cooperate with the investigation.
A charge-sheet has already been filed against other co- accused, while further investigation under Section 173(8) Cr.P.C. is pending in respect of the present respondent.

Even prior to being arrayed as an NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:31636 4 MCRC-28139-2025 accused, respondent No.2 had participated in the investigation, his statement was recorded, and he furnished relevant documents to the police.
Upon being added as an accused, he sought anticipatory bail, which was rightly allowed by the court below on 20.06.2025.
The co-accused Arvind Singh Bhadoriya and Jitendra Singh Chandel, who allegedly played a more active role in the offence, have already been granted regular bail by this Court.
Respondent No.2 further contends that the application for cancellation of bail incorrectly attributes to him the duty of verification based on the statement of Deputy Manager Subhash Dubey.

sentences.text: , in cases where loans range between Rs.25,00,000/- and Rs.50,00,000/-, the responsibility of conducting counselling, personal discussions, KYC verification, and business inspection lies with the Deputy Manager or Assistant Manager.

The respondent was serving merely as Area Manager, whereas officers Rohit Mangal and Akash Wadhwani were posted as Assistant Manager and Deputy Manager, respectively, and thus were responsible for carrying out the required procedural formalities.
Therefore, the assertion that respondent No.2 failed in his duty of verification is factually incorrect.
Even assuming for the sake of argument that being a superior officer he was required to ensure verification, criminal liability cannot be fastened upon him merely for supervisory lapses.
The respondent had no role in sanctioning or disbursing the loan.
On the contrary, he was the one who pointed out discrepancies and irregularities in the loan process and sent emails to higher officials on 27.09.2024 and on other occasions.

Acting upon these email communications, the higher NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:31636 5 MCRC-28139-2025 authorities of LIC Housing Finance
granted him permission through a communication dated 03.07.2025 to lodge an FIR regarding fraudulent loan disbursement.
In pursuance thereof, the respondent himself submitted an application to the Superintendent of Police for lodging the FIR.
Accordingly, it is prayed that the present application seeking cancellation of bail be dismissed.
Heard counsel for the parties and perusing the record.

The settled legal position governing cancellation of bail is that bail once granted may be cancelled only when the accused misuses the liberty granted to him, interferes with the investigation, attempts to evade the process of law,
tampers with witnesses, commits a similar offence or otherwise displays conduct that frustrates the course of justice.

The Supreme Court in Dolat Ram v. State of Haryana , (1995) 1 SCC 349, held that rejection of bail and cancellation of bail stand on different footings, and the bail already granted can be cancelled only on the basis of supervening circumstances or misuse of liberty.

entities.text: Dolat Ram v. State of Haryana , (1995) 1 SCC 349
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similarly, in X v.
State of Telangana , (2018) 16 SCC 511 , it has been reiterated that cancellation of bail cannot be sought merely because the order granting bail is alleged to be unjustified; the applicant must demonstrate actual misuse of liberty.

entities.text:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the above principles to the present case, it is not demonstrated that respondent No.2 has violated any condition of bail, interfered with the investigation or misused the liberty granted to him.
The investigating agency has not made any complaint of non-cooperation or obstruction after the grant of anticipatory bail.

The allegations relied on by NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:31636 6 MCRC-28139-2025 the applicant pertain to the merits of the case and the role of the respondent in the alleged conspiracy; however, such considerations are not relevant to an application for cancellation of bail in the absence of any subsequent misconduct.
The trial Court passed the impugned order after considering the material available at that stage and there is no allegation that the respondent has since abused the concession extended to him.

In view of the legal position and the factual matrix of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that no ground is made out to warrant cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to respondent No.2.
The application lacks merit and is accordingly dismissed.
